jess_support: FYI — escalation from AcmeMobile. They see SSE streams that cut out mid-response when users switch from WiFi -> cellular on iOS. Partial transcript chunks, sometimes a 403 on reconnect. Customer says it started yesterday after a small edge change. Request id: req_abc123. Can infra take a look?

mike_infra: Thanks Jess. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the server logs around req_abc123? Also which model/route and whether this is hosted or dedicated for Acme?

jess_support: Hosted. Model: redwood-chat-medium. Repro steps from customer: turn wifi off during an active stream (iOS foreground). Attached log snippet they saved: ```
[2025-04-05T15:22:11.842Z] request=req_abc123 route=/v1/streams model=redwood-chat-medium state=streaming token_emitted=512
[2025-04-05T15:22:13.101Z] upstream=edge-proxy status=499 summary="client closed"
[2025-04-05T15:22:13.105Z] auth=403 message="token expired on reconnect"
[2025-04-05T15:22:13.106Z] stream=partial_chunk count=1 last_chunk="{\"content\":\"...I think we should\"}"
```
Minimal client request they used (curl SSE): ```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-chat-medium&conversation_id=acme-1"
```
They say when they toggle wifi quickly the client sees the connection close and a subsequent reconnect returns 403 because the token was rotated on the server side.

sara_sre: Two likely factors: 1) edge-proxy idle/keepalive settings + conn close semantics on iOS, 2) token TTL/rotation timing. The 499 upstream=client closed indicates the client sent FIN/RST before server finished. If the refresh token flow is racing with reconnect, we can see 403 on the next attempt. Can infra check proxy timeouts (proxy_read_timeout, keepalive_timeout) and the token rotation window for streaming tokens? Also check whether we emit a specific close reason in our SSE footers.

alex_mobile: iOS notes: switching networks kills in-flight HTTP/2 streams in the OS and the app often gets a clean close with no data. In practice, the app should detect network change (NWPathMonitor) and attempt a short, aggressive reconnect with conversation_id + resume token. On mobile we avoid re-authing on network change if possible — refresh tokens can be preemptively fetched before the reconnect attempt. Example reconnect pseudo: ```
onNetworkChange() {
  if (activeStream) {
    // short backoff -> try resume with same conversation_id
    wait(200ms); reconnect(keepConversation=true, keepPrefixCache=true);
  }
}
```
This reduces races during token rotation.

luis_support: Billing question from Acme: do we bill for partial responses if the client disconnects mid-stream? They want to know if they were charged for the truncated transcript.

billing-bot: Short answer: tokens emitted to the client are billable. If the server aborted due to an infra bug (e.g., proxy config causing premature closes) we can evaluate credits case-by-case. Please open a support ticket with request ids and timestamps (we have req_abc123) and we'll review for a manual credit. See: https://redwood.ai/docs/billing#partial-outputs

deploy-bot: Rollout note: edge-proxy config change rolled out yesterday at 14:50 UTC — we lowered keepalive_timeout from 60s -> 15s to address a scaling issue. The change affected a subset of edge nodes (zone eu-west-1). This could explain shorter-lived SSE connections. Change id: changelist/5123.

mike_infra: Ok actionable plan: 1) Roll back keepalive_timeout change on eu-west edge nodes immediately and monitor midstream disconnect metric (owner: mike_infra) — ETA 30m. 2) Patch auth service to extend streaming-token grace window by +10s on rotation to allow quick reconnect after network flaps (owner: sara_sre) — target hotfix in 4h. 3) Add server-side log annotation when we close a stream due to upstream proxy teardown so we can distinguish client FIN vs proxy drop (owner: infra-observability) — next-day. 4) Support docs: update mobile SDK guidance with reconnect/resume snippet (owner: alex_mobile + luis_support) — next week. 5) If customer requests, issue billing review for req_abc123 (owner: billing-bot + jess_support).

jess_support: Thanks — I'll tell Acme: rollback underway, ETA for hotfix ~4h, and we'll follow up on credits if any. Also sharing their quick repro (wifi toggle during active stream) and asking them to capture a packet trace if possible. Will keep thread posted. :thumbsup:

mike_infra: Rolling back edge change now (started 15:04 UTC). Will post metrics in 20m.

sara_sre: I'll start the auth grace-window hotfix and push to canary. If we confirm proxy was culprit we'll still recommend client reconnection best-practices in SDK.

jess_support: Closing loop with customer: "we identified an edge config change that can prematurely tear long-lived SSE; we've rolled back and are deploying a short auth grace-window fix. Please retry and paste any new req ids if you see more disconnects."
